method.method_draft: Use only proportional comparisons instead of assigning concrete dimensions. From the image, note that the three right-hand rectangles share the same width and together span the full height, while the left rectangle spans the full height. Because the three right rectangles have equal area and equal width, their heights are equal, so each has height one-third of the flag height. Let the whole flag have height H and width W. Let the left rectangle have width x and the right stack have width y. Equal area between the left rectangle and one right rectangle gives xH = y(H/3), so y = 3x. Hence W = x + y = 4x, so y = 3W/4. The white rectangle has height H/3 and width 3W/4. Using the text ratio H:W = 3:5, its side ratio is H/3 : 3W/4 = 4H : 9W = 4·3 : 9·5 = 12:45 = 4:15.
